gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: This is the house in ___ I was born.
gaps.explanation: 'In which' is the formal pattern; 'in where' does not exist and 'in that' is impossible in relative clauses.

gaps.sentence: That's the office ___ I worked for ten years.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which'; 'I worked the office' shows the place role of the gap.

gaps.sentence: Show me ___ you have written so far.
gaps.explanation: 'What you have written' means 'the things that you have written'; 'that' cannot head a nominal clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: This is the beach ___ we used to play as children.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces place information; 'we used to play' already has a subject and object, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The book ___ I borrowed from the library is two weeks overdue.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things; 'who' refers only to people and 'where' to places.
